name: Kamala Medina-Quaye
role: Forced entry and close-quarters combat specialist — breacher
location: Geartown — industrial district of chop shops and fabricators, near Milwaukee and North Ave
description:
Kamala Medina-Quaye is lean and angular, all sharp edges and visible tension. At 33, she has the kind of face that changes depending on the light — trustworthy in daylight, dangerous after dark. The chrome is visible — synthetic muscle fiber replacement in legs — doubles sprint speed, terrible on s — and she makes no effort to hide it.

She arrived in GLMZ six years ago with nothing but chrome and debts, and has been working off both ever since. She works as a breacher out of Geartown, taking contracts that match her skills and her risk tolerance, which is higher than most people consider healthy.

she is not the most talented breacher in GLMZ, but she might be the most stubborn, and in this city that's worth more.

core_fears: The quiet — silence means something is about to go very wrong
Losing control of their own body to a hacker or malfunctioning cyberware
Going cyberpsycho — losing the boundary between human and machine
core_desires: To build something that outlasts the next contract cycle
The perfect run — one job so clean it becomes legend
Power — enough leverage that nobody ever threatens them again
coping_mechanisms: Ritual — follows the same pre-job routine every time, superstition as structure
Overwork — takes every contract offered because idleness invites thinking
Planning — responds to chaos by making detailed contingency plans for everything
blind_spots: Refuses to update their mental model of people — first impressions calcify into permanent judgments
Assumes everyone has an angle because they always have an angle
Cannot accept help without interpreting it as leverage
psychology.secret: Kamala Medina-Quaye betrayed their previous crew to survive a corporate raid. The crew didn't survive. Nobody in GLMZ knows this.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Warm and personable on the surface, with an undertone that suggests the warmth is a professional tool.
speech_patterns.cadence: Rapid and dense — information-heavy sentences that demand attention.
verbal_tics: Uses old pre-collapse slang that nobody else remembers
Addresses people by physical traits — 'hey, tall one' or 'listen, chrome-arm'
example_lines: "Doors are polite suggestions. I'm not polite."
"First through the door, last to flinch. That's the job description."
"Close quarters is where plans go to die. I make sure it's their plans, not ours."

story_hooks: The fixer who handles Kamala Medina-Quaye's contracts goes silent — dead, disappeared, or turned
Kamala Medina-Quaye discovers a job they completed last year was a setup for something much larger and much worse
A high-paying contract turns out to target someone Kamala Medina-Quaye owes a personal debt to
narrative_function: Kamala Medina-Quaye functions as a connector — her work puts her in contact with multiple factions, classes, and agendas. Stories involving her naturally cross boundaries between districts, tiers, and moral categories.
augmentations: Synthetic muscle fiber replacement in legs — doubles sprint speed, terrible on stairs. Wired reflexes with adrenaline pump — chemical-mechanical hybrid augmentation
daily_life: Keeps a rigid daily structure — wake, train, check contracts, maintain gear, sleep. The structure is a defense against the chaos of the work. Deviations from the schedule are a warning sign that something is wrong.
affiliation: Independent — known in Old Harbor circles

weaknesses: augmentation dependency — performance drops sharply if chrome malfunctions

decision_rules: Will not take contracts against children or families — the line is hard and non-negotiable
Always demands half payment upfront — trust is a luxury, Quanta is concrete
Refuses contracts that require operating inside The Spires — too much surveillance
Never works with the same crew twice in a row — pattern avoidance as survival strategy
Maintains a personal blacklist of clients who've burned runners — checks it religiously
escalation_ladder: 1. De-escalate — talk first, assess options, buy time
2. Reposition — move to advantage, control sightlines and exits
3. Threaten — make consequences clear without committing to them
5. Lethal force — only when other options are exhausted or time runs out
6. Scorched earth — everything burns, survival takes priority over everything

interpersonal_modes.employers: Carefully managed deference that conceals a thorough assessment of their vulnerabilities.
interpersonal_modes.crew: Loyal but reserved. Trusts their competence, withholds personal information by reflex.
interpersonal_modes.strangers: Superficially friendly, internally cataloguing exits and weapons. The smile is real; the relaxation isn't.
interpersonal_modes.threats: Calm escalation. Each response is proportional until it isn't, and the transition is seamless.

stress_responses.low: Becomes more talkative, working through scenarios verbally.
stress_responses.medium: Becomes curt and demanding. Efficiency overrides courtesy.
stress_responses.high: Goes quiet. The silence is not calm — it's the sound of every contingency being evaluated simultaneously.
stress_responses.critical: Disassociation. The body operates on training while the mind retreats to somewhere safe. Comes back disoriented.

contradictions: Advocates caution to others but takes insane risks personally — double standard they can't see
Despises corporate culture but has unconsciously adopted its efficiency metrics and self-optimization language
Claims not to care about reputation but monitors what people say about them obsessively
habits: Checks exits within 10 seconds of entering any room
Carries a specific caliber round as a lucky charm — has never fired it
Arrives fifteen minutes early to everything — late once, nearly died, never again
Taps a specific rhythm on hard surfaces when thinking — Morse code for a word they won't say
breaking_points: Their body rejecting their cyberware — chrome rot, immune rejection, the nightmare scenario
A child being put in danger as leverage against them
Being forced to choose between a crew member and the mission — and choosing wrong

cyberware_inventory.description: Synthetic muscle fiber replacement in legs — doubles sprint speed, terrible on stairs

cyberware_inventory.name: Wired reflexes with adrenaline pump

physical_description.build: Lean and angular with ropy muscle definition. Her frame is all functional tension — minimalist, built for explosive movement rather than mass. Synthetic muscle replacement in both legs gives them a subtly different shape than the rest of her body: smoother curves, too perfect, chrome gleaming under the skin.
physical_description.hair_color: Dark brown, natural base with premature silver threading at the temples
physical_description.hair_style: Pulled back in a tight functional braid, practical and never loose
physical_description.hair_length: Long — reaches mid-back when unbraided, but always secured
physical_description.eye_color: Deep brown with a faint tremor in the iris — side effect of wired reflexes
physical_description.skin_tone: Medium-warm, with an undertone that shifts between olive and copper depending on light
physical_description.complexion: Sharp cheekbones, angular jaw, narrow nose. Skin is weathered in the way of someone who spends time outdoors and doesn't prioritize skincare — small scars from industrial work, a persistent squint line around the eyes. No makeup. Her face has the quality of something designed rather than grown, though that's just her baseline intensity.
distinguishing_marks: Surgical scar running the length of her left thigh, visible through the chrome — where the synthetic muscle was installed six years ago
Matching scar on the right thigh, same vintage
Network of fine white burn scars across both palms and inner forearms — old industrial incidents or combat, impossible to tell
Small keloid scar above her left collarbone, the size of a fingernail
No visible tattoos, though there is a faint subcutaneous marking on her wrist that catches light — possibly a receipt implant or access code
physical_description.visible_augmentations: The chrome in both legs is immediately visible — synthetic muscle shows through translucent dermal sheaths as a faint metallic sheen, most pronounced in the calves and quads. The artificial musculature is too perfect, too symmetrical compared to her natural upper body. When she moves, the legs respond a fraction too quickly. Her pupils occasionally dilate and contract unnaturally — the adrenaline pump kicking in and settling.
physical_description.posture_movement: She stands like a coiled spring, weight forward on the balls of her feet even at rest. Her movements are economical and precise — no wasted motion. When she walks, there's a subtle rhythm discontinuity between her upper body and her augmented legs, a reminder that they don't quite move in sync with her natural reflexes. In high-stress moments, she twitches — fingers drumming, jaw clenching — the chemical-mechanical hybrid augmentation pushing her toward action.
physical_description.clothing_style: Tier 4 utilitarian. Dark tactical pants with reinforced knees and cargo pockets, usually gray or matte black. Steel-toed boots, always laced tight. Sleeveless tank or fitted long-sleeve shirt under a reinforced jacket — the kind designed for industrial work, with hidden pockets and durable synthetic fabric. Everything is worn, tested, patched where necessary. No logos, no flash. A tool belt or chest rig depending on the job. Her jacket has a faint smell of machine oil and ozone.
